edits.text: 3. SEVERANCE; CAUSE; GOOD REASON. If the Company terminates the Executive's employment without Cause, other than by reason of death or disability, or the Executive resigns for Good Reason, the Company shall pay severance equal to two times the Executive's annual Base Salary plus one target annual bonus, each at the rate in effect immediately before termination, disregarding any reduction giving rise to Good Reason. Target annual bonus means the annual target amount expressly agreed in writing under Section 2, not a maximum or discretionary above-target award. Severance is subject to required withholding and the Executive's execution and non-revocation of a mutually acceptable release of claims. The release shall exclude claims that cannot lawfully be released, rights under this Agreement, vested benefits, and applicable indemnification and insurance rights. The Company shall deliver the release within seven days after termination; it must become effective and irrevocable within 60 days after termination, subject to legally required consideration and revocation periods. Cash severance shall be paid in a lump sum on the first regular payroll date following the 60th day after termination, subject to any delay required by applicable law. If that release period spans two taxable years, payment shall not occur before the second taxable year. The Executive shall not select the taxable year of payment. For 24 months following termination, the Company shall also continue the Executive's and eligible dependents' medical, dental and vision coverage at Company expense, subject to timely continuation-coverage elections where required. If continuation under the plans is unavailable or unlawful, the Company shall instead provide a lawful cash substitute based on the cost of comparable coverage, without any tax gross-up. This continuation or substitute shall cease upon eligibility for comparable coverage through a new employer, which the Executive shall promptly report. Accrued salary, vested benefits, reimbursable business expenses and other amounts required by applicable law remain payable independently of the release. 'Cause' means: (i) conviction of, or plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony involving fraud or dishonesty materially related to the Executive's duties; (ii) fraud, embezzlement or willful misconduct in performing those duties that causes material harm to the Company; or (iii) a willful and material breach of this Agreement or continued willful failure to perform material lawful duties after written notice specifying the breach or failure and 30 days to cure, if curable. Cause shall require a good-faith determination by the Board after written notice and a reasonable opportunity for the Executive to be heard with counsel. Mere poor performance or a good-faith business judgment shall not constitute Cause. 'Good Reason' means, without the Executive's written consent: (a) a material reduction in Base Salary or the agreed target annual bonus; (b) a material diminution in the Executive's authority, duties or responsibilities; (c) relocation of the principal work location by more than 50 miles that materially increases the Executive's commute; or (d) a material breach of this Agreement by the Company. Good Reason requires written notice specifying the condition within 90 days after its initial occurrence, failure by the Company to cure within 30 days after receipt, and resignation within 30 days after expiration of the cure period. Payments shall be administered to comply with applicable law, including Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code where applicable; any required six-month delay for a specified employee shall apply only to the extent legally necessary, with delayed amounts paid promptly after that period.
edits.name: Severance and termination definitions

edits.text: 4. CONFIDENTIALITY; NO POST-EMPLOYMENT NON-COMPETE. No post-employment non-compete or non-solicitation restriction is imposed by this Agreement. The Executive shall not use or disclose the Company's Confidential Information except in performing duties for the Company or as authorized in writing. 'Confidential Information' means nonpublic information learned through employment concerning the Company's trade secrets, source code, product development, security credentials, nonpublic financial results or forecasts, and confidential customer contract terms, in each case that the Company takes reasonable measures to protect. It excludes information that becomes public without breach, was lawfully known to the Executive without a duty of confidence, is independently developed without use of Confidential Information, or is lawfully received from a third party without a duty of confidence. General skills, experience and knowledge are not restricted. These obligations last for two years after employment ends, except that trade secrets remain protected only for so long as they qualify as trade secrets under applicable law. Upon termination, the Executive shall return Company property and Confidential Information, but may retain personal compensation and benefit records and records reasonably necessary to enforce legal rights, subject to this Section. Nothing prohibits disclosures required by law, confidential communications with counsel, reporting suspected violations to governmental or regulatory authorities, participating in investigations, protected discussion of employment terms, or other legally protected activity; no prior authorization or notice to the Company is required for protected reporting. Under 18 U.S.C. Section 1833(b), an individual is not liable under federal or state trade-secret law for confidential disclosure of a trade secret to a government official or an attorney solely to report or investigate a suspected violation of law, or for disclosure in a complaint or other document filed under seal. An individual pursuing a retaliation claim for reporting a suspected violation may disclose trade secrets to counsel and use them in the proceeding if filings containing them are under seal and disclosure occurs only as permitted by court order. The governing jurisdiction shall be mutually agreed and inserted before execution; this Section shall not restrict conduct protected by applicable law.
edits.name: Replace non-compete with confidentiality
